table.name: singer
table.purpose: One row per singer/artist, with personal and financial attributes; referenced by the song table via Singer_ID. Note: the 'Name' values (Christy Walton, Alice Walton, Iris Fontbona, Gina Rinehart, etc.) are actually names of wealthy businesspeople/billionaires, not singers, so the data appears synthetic or mislabeled despite the table name and join structure suggesting singers.

Birth_Year.name: Birth_Year
Birth_Year.description: Year of birth of the person (1940-1962).

Citizenship.name: Citizenship
Citizenship.description: Country of citizenship (e.g. United States, Australia, Chile, France, Germany).

Name.name: Name
Name.description: Full name of the person. Values are names of well-known billionaires (Christy Walton, Alice Walton, Iris Fontbona, Gina Rinehart, etc.), inconsistent with a table of singers; likely synthetic sample data. The join structure (songs referencing these rows as their singers) supports the column being the person's name, but not whether these are genuinely singers.

Net_Worth_Millions.name: Net_Worth_Millions
Net_Worth_Millions.description: Net worth in millions of (presumably US) dollars, ranging 12.7 to 30.0.

Singer_ID.name: Singer_ID
Singer_ID.description: Primary key identifying each singer; referenced by song.Singer_ID.

table.name: song
table.purpose: One row per song, with its title, sales, chart performance, and the singer who performed it (foreign key to singer).

Highest_Position.name: Highest_Position
Highest_Position.description: Highest chart position reached by the song (1 = number one; values 1 and 3).

Sales.name: Sales
Sales.description: Sales figure for the song, in units/copies (261,000 to 1,094,000).

Singer_ID.name: Singer_ID
Singer_ID.description: Foreign key to singer.Singer_ID identifying the performing singer; some singers have multiple songs.

Title.name: Title
Title.description: Title of the song (e.g. 'Cha Cha Slide', 'Do They Know It's Christmas').
